title: The definability of objective becoming in Minkowski spacetime
relevance: Direct predecessor: Theorem 1 (p.365) trichotomy {chronological past, causal past, universal} for absolute becoming in Minkowski under definability, transitivity and chronological becoming; Lemma p.364; Theorem 2 (pp.371-372) worldline-dependent version; final-section remark (pp.385-386) that no extension beyond Minkowski is obvious. The audited manuscript's thm:flat reproduces Theorem 1 as the Minkowski instance of the becoming-theory axioms.
limits: Springer paywall; PhilArchive/PhilPapers full text and PhilSci copies blocked from this environment. Content verified only through the publisher abstract/PhilPapers abstract and Savitt's verbatim secondary rendering with page locators (pa-savitt-cdlp). Primary pages 365-367 and 385-386 NOT read in this run; the manuscript's direct quotations of pp.385-386 remain unverified against the primary text. title: On relativity theory and openness of the future
version: Philosophy of Science 58 (1991) 147-167; JSTOR scan, 21 pages, downloaded 2026-10-25
section_locator: Theorem stated p.149; symmetry proof pp.149-150; definability requirement p.149; GR remarks pp.159, 166
relevance: Restates and proves the Minkowski uniqueness theorem: reflexive+transitive R invariant under time-orientation-preserving automorphisms, nontrivial in the past-causal direction, implies R = past causal connectibility. Proof is purely symmetry-based (spacelike pairs related -> universal). Confirms the audited manuscript's reading that Stein's argument runs entirely on single-spacetime symmetry and contains no curved-spacetime or cross-spacetime claim.
limits: Scan read in full; no machine text layer. Stein's 'definable in terms of Einstein-Minkowski geometry' is used informally; no category, no naturality across spacetimes.

title: On the paradoxical time-structures of Gödel
relevance: Contains, at p.594, Stein's explicitly posed deformation question: whether a cosmological model can be continuously deformed, through Einstein-compatible intermediate states, to a state with Gödel-type relationships (verified verbatim via Manchak 2017, pa-manchak2017). The closest Stein-side ancestor of cross-spacetime reasoning; about Gödel-type causal relations, not becoming relations.
limits: Cambridge/JSTOR paywall; read at abstract plus the verbatim p.594 quotation in Manchak. No theorem about becoming; no local covariance. Note: this is a different paper from Stein's other 1970 note (J. Philos. 67:289-294); both are 'Stein 1970' in parts of the literature.

title: A note on time and relativity theory
version: Journal of Philosophy 67 (1970) 289-294; scan text extracted via search rendering
relevance: Reply to Lango on invariance of 'relativistic instantaneous cross sections'; shows Stein's care about automorphism-invariance vs permutability. Confirms there is no deformation or GR-becoming content in this note (it is the other 'Stein 1970').
limits: Content read through the search-engine text rendering of the scan; clarifies the two-Stein-1970 disambiguation.

title: Not-so-absolute cosmic simultaneity
version: Erkenntnis, first online 2026-03-09, open access; PhilSci-Archive preprint 28022 PDF read in full (26 pages); received 2025-04-07, accepted 2026-01-27
relevance: Named anchor. Defines the Causal Connection Condition (CCC, p.7): a temporal relation is absolute only if it obtains independently of any causally disconnected event; shows metaphysical cosmic simultaneity violates CCC. Contains no becoming theorem, no classification, no local-covariance formalism; cites Stein 1968/1970/1991 as a suggestion (p.19) and never cites Clifton-Hogarth. Confirms the manuscript's use of Viglione as an informal locality intuition, and confirms CCC is conceptually adjacent to (LC) but never formalized.
limits: Published-version-of-record pagination not checked (Springer blocked); preprint read in full. 0 citations at check date.

title: What becomes of a causal set?
version: Author draft dated 30 January 2015 (= arXiv:1502.00018v1), 15 pages, read in full; published BJPS 68 (2017) 907-925, doi:10.1093/bjps/axv040 not separately diffed
section_locator: Section 3: counterexample causet d<b,c<a and automorphism-invariant relation R; footnote 5 ('could be a small proper part of a much larger causet'); 'The analogue of this theorem, however, is straightforwardly false in CST' (opening of the counterexample discussion)
relevance: Establishes the per-structure failure of the Stein analogue in CST and the non-Hegelian-pair diagnosis. Contains no embedding category, no convex-embedding morphisms, no cross-structure theorem; footnote 5 states the part-of-larger-causet possibility without proving anything. The audited prop:causets (exact Stein theorem on locally finite posets with convex order-embeddings) is a different, stronger-hypothesis result and is not in this paper.
limits: Draft version read; the published version may differ in pagination/wording (manuscript cites §3 and footnote 5, both present in the draft).

title: The philosophy of causal set theory
version: arXiv:2308.05217v1 (2023-08-09); Handbook of Quantum Gravity (Springer 2024), doi:10.1007/978-981-99-7681-2_71
section_locator: Section 3 and references; keyword scan of full text: 'convex' 0 hits, 'embed' 1 hit, 'Stein' 8 hits (all restating Stein 1991/WC2017)

title: The generally covariant locality principle - a new paradigm for local quantum physics
section_locator: Section 2: category Man = four-dimensional oriented, time-oriented globally hyperbolic spacetimes; morphisms = isometric embeddings with (i) causally convex image (any causal curve in the target with endpoints in the image lies in the image) and (ii) orientation and time-orientation preservation; Definition (i) locally covariant QFT as covariant functor Man->Alg; Definition: local covariant field as natural transformation
relevance: Source of the exact category and naturality condition the audited theorem transplants to becoming relations. The locality hypothesis (LC) of the manuscript is BFV naturality; BFV applies it to *-algebras, never to transitive relations or preorders, and contains no Stein-type classification.
limits: Definitions and surrounding text read from arXiv HTML; full 34-page proof apparatus not audited (not needed for the priority question).

title: Dynamical locality and covariance: what makes a physical theory the same in all spacetimes?
section_locator: Principles S1 (every candidate theory class should be locally covariant) and S2 (subtheories isomorphic in one spacetime should be isomorphic in all) from the introduction via ar5iv rendering
relevance: Nearest structural precedent for the manuscript's cross-spacetime logic: S2 has the same 'verdict in one spacetime propagates to all spacetimes' shape, formulated for subtheory isomorphisms, and Fewster-Verch prove the class of all locally covariant theories fails it (dynamical locality rescues a sub-class), plus a no-go on natural states. Related work 1201.3195 (Fewster-Verch endomorphisms/automorphisms) classifies functor automorphisms, not preorders. Neither contains a Stein-type classification of natural transitive relations.
limits: Abstract plus the S1/S2 statement and Loc-category definition (footnote 3) read from ar5iv rendering; full 60-page paper not read in this run. Flagged as the under-used nearest mathematical neighbor.

title: Temporal becoming in a relativistic universe: causal diamonds and Gödel's philosophy of time
version: Eur. J. Philos. Sci. 12:44 (2022); PhilSci-Archive 20665 preprint
relevance: Defends local (causal-diamond) becoming and a defense of Gödel's modal step; conceptual. Modifies the causal-diamond present for spacetimes with CTCs. No classification theorem; no cross-spacetime formalism. Confirms the manuscript's prior-work characterization.

title: A remark on 'time machines' in honor of Howard Stein
version: Presented at The Philosophy of Howard Stein conference, University of Chicago, 2017-06-09; PhilSci-Archive 15123 PDF

relevance: Documents Stein's own explicitly posed cross-model question and the subsequent time-machine framework (Earman 1995; Earman-Smeenk-Wüthrich 2009; Krasnikov; Manchak 2009-2014; Smeenk-Wüthrich). Shows the deformation program concerns Gödel-type causal structure, not becoming relations, and never formulates a local-covariance classification.
